title: Home Mortgage Loans Rate and Lock Sheet: Published Note Rates, Lock Periods and the Closing Timetable
content:
The rates below are the currently published note rates for Home Mortgage Loans at zero points for a 45-day lock. Beside each rate this sheet carries the number of calendar days a locked rate is honored before closing, the number of calendar days after application within which the loan must close, and the timetable on which the first installment falls due.

| Program | Published note rate | Lock honored | Loan must close within | First installment falls due | Due day of month |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FHA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 6.125 percent | 45 calendar days | 60 calendar days after application | 2 calendar months after the funding month | 1 |
| VA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 5.875 percent | 45 calendar days | 60 calendar days after application | 2 calendar months after the funding month | 1 |
| Conventional 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 6.375 percent | 45 calendar days | 60 calendar days after application | 2 calendar months after the funding month | 1 |
| Conventional 15-Year Fixed Mortgage | 5.625 percent | 45 calendar days | 60 calendar days after application | 2 calendar months after the funding month | 1 |
| 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage | 5.990 percent | 45 calendar days | 60 calendar days after application | 2 calendar months after the funding month | 1 |
| Jumbo 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | 6.500 percent | 45 calendar days | 75 calendar days after application | 2 calendar months after the funding month | 1 |

## Notes to the sheet

The published rate is quoted at zero points and for a lock of 45 calendar days; the lock period is the same 45 calendar days on every program.

The closing window is 60 calendar days on five of the programs and 75 calendar days on the Jumbo 30-Year Fixed Mortgage, which is the one program allowed a longer window.

Installments fall due on the first day of the month on every program, and the first of them falls in the month 2 calendar months after the month in which the loan funded.

## Worked illustration of the timetable

Take a hypothetical Conventional 30-Year Fixed Mortgage that funds in March. Counting 2 calendar months forward from the funding month reaches May, and the due day of the month is the first, so the first installment of that hypothetical loan falls due on 1 May. Had the same loan funded in December, the first installment would fall due on 1 February of the following year.
